en.title: Everyday questions
en.goal: Ask a variety of open questions: who, why, where someone lives or works, whether there is something in a place.

lessons.apresentar-trabalho: Introducing someone and saying where they work

dialogue.title: Introducing a friend
lines: This is my girlfriend, she's a student.
Where does she work or study?
She studies at the school, and there are some of her books here.

shei.title: 谁 (shéi) — asking "who"
shei.body: 谁 (shéi) asks about a person, and it takes the same place in the sentence that the answer would — if the answer is "I" at the start of the sentence, 谁 also goes at the start.

weishenme-yinwei.title: "Wèishénme" or "yīnwèi"?
weishenme-yinwei.body: Wèishénme (为什么) is the question: "why?". Yīnwèi (因为) is the answer: "because". They always go together, as a pair.

meiyou-de.title: Close possession without 的
meiyou-de.body: For very close personal relationships (family, boyfriend/girlfriend), Chinese sometimes leaves out the 的 that would normally mark possession.

difang-you.title: Place + 有 + Object — saying what exists in a place
difang-you.body: To say that something exists in a certain place ("there's coffee here"), the structure is: Place + 有 + Object — the place comes first, whereas English often puts it at the end ("there's coffee here").

difang-you.title: 一些 (yìxiē) — "some" or "a bit of"
difang-you.body: 一些 (yìxiē) indicates a small, non-specific amount of something — it equals "some" (countable things) or "a bit of" (uncountable things, like liquids).

zai-difang-verb.title: 在 + Place + Verb — where the action happens
zai-difang-verb.body: When you want to say where an action happens (not just where something is sitting), 在 + Place goes before the verb — different from when 在 alone only shows the position of something.

trueFalse.claim: This question asks where someone lives.
trueFalse.whyNote: Wrong — 你为什么不去？ asks for the REASON (为什么 = why) for not going, not where the person lives. "Where do you live?" would be "你住在哪里？".
